prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key policies and commitments (2010)

Economy and public finances
- Support the recovery now; more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, fair tax measures and cuts to lower-priority spending.
- Efficiency and pay discipline: major back-office savings; cap basic public-sector pay uplifts at 1% in 2011–13; reform public-sector pensions; asset sales by 2020.
- No rises in basic or higher income tax rates; maintain protections on VAT-exempt essentials.

Banking and business
- Stronger bank regulation: higher capital, “living wills,” clampdown on risky remuneration, global levy, and actions to boost competition and mutuals.
- Realise stakes in state-supported banks to protect taxpayers.
- UK Finance for Growth (£4bn) to channel capital to SMEs and high-tech firms; R&D tax credits, patent box, Strategic Investment Fund.
- Small Business Credit Adjudicator; Time to Pay; one-year small business rates holiday; double Entrepreneurs’ Relief limit.

Jobs, welfare and skills
- Job guarantees: roles or training for young people after six months; mandatory job offer after two years’ unemployment.
- Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee.
- Expand advanced apprenticeships; Skills Accounts; right to request time for training.

Infrastructure and industry
- High Speed Rail linking major cities; Crossrail completion; rail electrification; enforceable right to the cheapest rail fare.
- Green Investment Bank; extended hard-shoulder running; no national road pricing; Heathrow third runway with strict conditions; 100,000 EV charging points.
- Universal broadband (2 Mbps by 2012), phased superfast rollout; fixed-line levy to reach final 10%.

Housing and consumer finance
- Stamp duty holiday for first-time buyers under £250k (two years); 5% rate on homes over £1m.
- Strengthen mortgage regulation under the FSA; expand affordable/social housing and reform council housing finance; landlord register and private renting standards.
- Transform Post Office into a People’s Bank; universal basic bank account right; curb high-cost lending; single consumer finance regulator.

Education
- Protect frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools, and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places.
- One-to-one/small-group tuition guarantees; parent “trigger” to change school leadership; up to 1,000 schools in accredited groups by 2015.
- Personal tutors in secondary; diplomas and stronger vocational routes; raise participation to 18; expand advanced apprenticeships; widen university access.

NHS and care
- Protect NHS spending; legally binding patient guarantees (18-week treatment; one-week cancer test results; routine health checks 40–74).
- Any Qualified Provider choice at NHS prices; more home-based care; expand psychological therapies.
- Empower staff; drive efficiencies for reinvestment; strengthen infection control.
- National Care Service: free home care for highest needs from 2011; cap residential care costs after two years from 2014.

Policing, justice and immigration
- Maintain police and PCSO numbers; neighbourhood teams visible 80% of the time; online force report cards; enable takeovers of failing forces.
- Faster, tougher action on anti-social behaviour with a right to injunctions for repeat victims.
- Use CCTV and DNA within safeguards; expand Community Payback.
- Points-based immigration system; stronger borders; pre-entry English tests; link settlement to contribution and compliance.

Culture, sport, environment
- 2012 Olympics legacy; school sport expansion; empower supporter trusts in football.
- Maintain free museum entry; protect pubs and post offices; uphold BBC independence; digital/broadband rollout.
- Target ~40% low-carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; renewables, nuclear, CCS; “pay-as-you-save” home retrofits; move toward zero waste; expand habitats and woodlands; supermarket ombudsman; rural broadband.

Constitution and localism
- Referendums on Alternative Vote and an elected second chamber; fixed-term parliaments; lobbying register; recall for serious misconduct; review voting age after enhanced citizenship education.
- More local control (Total Place), open data “Domesday Book,” stronger city-region powers; urban transport upgrades; keep council tax rises low.

International, defence and development
- Afghanistan strategy focused on protecting the population and training local forces; Strategic Defence Review; maintain independent deterrent; enhanced forces’ welfare.
- Active role in EU and global institutions; climate diplomacy; meet 0.7% aid target by 2013 in law; drive progress on health, education, governance, and fair trade.
